title: Choose the visual world for your portfolio
question: Fresh hand. The roll assigned the Punched-Card Deck. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Punched-Card Deck
options.lineage: 80-column punched cards and batch job decks
options.thesis: Your portfolio is a job deck: each system you shipped is one punched card, and the live demo punches a doctor's messy dictation into a structured card, column by column.
materials: card stock with printed column grid
punched holes showing the saturated blue ground
options.viewport: A drenched card-reader blue field; a giant punched card carries your name in printed caps with the holes spelling it in the column grid; the deck fans out below, ready to feed.
options.risk: Retro-computing nostalgia if the cards stay static; the card stock must not drift into beige.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale alone: the name is set enormous against tiny column numbers, no badges.
Keyboard-first: every card, the demo, and the deck can be driven from the keyboard.
Whole-unit borders: the column grid repeats in whole cells at every width, never cropped.
Numbered steps: every pipeline stage carries a circled step number on the card it punches.

options.label: Agent Transit Map
options.thesis: Your LangGraph pipelines drawn as a metro map: agents are stations, the validation loop is a circle line, and each project is a line you can ride.
options.viewport: Full-width map whose central interchange is your name; lines leave toward Projects, Demo, Skills, Contact.
options.risk: The most familiar hand here; diagram-as-map portfolios are a known move.

options.label: Depth Dive
options.lineage: technical dive logs and dive computers
options.thesis: Scroll is depth: recruiter summary at the surface, architecture and code the deeper you go, with a depth gauge ruling the page.
options.viewport: Turquoise surface with your name; a depth gauge on the edge starts at 0 m.
options.case: Matches the one-minute scan, ten-minute depth principle; loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Ocean theme has no tie to the actual work.

options.label: Annotated Reference Edition
options.thesis: Your work set as a dense two-column edition with a vermilion key rail and architecture notes hanging in the margin.
materials: hairline rules drawn by a ruling engine
options.viewport: Two columns of project text, the margin carrying LangGraph notes bracketed to their lines.
options.case: Engineering leads get real depth; loses on boldness and recruiter scanning.
options.risk: Lands in the editorial-serif look many AI pages ship.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.case: It is the dark-glow look you asked to leave.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: A giant letter morphs under a slider.
options.viewport: One giant glyph and an axis slider.
options.case: Speaks to type designers, not your audiences.
options.risk: Nothing about AI or clinical work.

options.label: Sewing Pattern Envelope
options.viewport: An envelope front with three views.

options.label: Pastel Mascot Sheet
options.thesis: A cute mascot with medical accessories.
options.case: Medical-grimness humour is wrong for clinical software.
options.kept: Borders that repeat in whole units.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern developer portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role, primary CTA, project grid below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other engineer's portfolio by design.
